t: named him, by a by-name, surname,
nickname; he by-named him, surnamed him,
named him, by a nickname, a name of reproach,
: (K:) or the latter is with teshdeed to denote muchness, or frequency, or repetition, of the action, or its application to many objects: you say,
They called one another by by-names, surnames,
calling one another by names of reproach.
(TA.) So in the Kur, xlix. 11; where the doing so is forbidden. (TA.)
[or, accord. to the Msb, it seems to be
, for it is there said to be an inf. n. used as a subst., but this form I have never met with elsewhere,]
a name of reproach; an opprobrious appellation:
(TA:) but Kh, [makes it, contr. to common usage, to signify
for he] says, that names are of two kinds;
in his grounds of pretension to respect,
quality, and in his natural disposition.
A man who is much accustomed to call others by by-names, surnames,

mufradat: النبز: التلقيب. قال الله تعالى: ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب [الحجرات/ 11] .
